title: From hard-core to soft-core bosons in a shell trap
authors: G. Costa, S. Prestipino, F. Cinti, M. Ciardi
abstract: We study the low-temperature states of a system of spinless bosons trapped in a broad spherical shell. In our virtual (path-integral Monte Carlo) experiments, we specifically examine how the equilibrium structure and overall superfluidity of the system are affected by a change of the interparticle-potential core from hard to increasingly soft. In this manner we bridge the gap between the behaviors of two species of bosons: Helium-like atoms, which self-assemble into ordinary crystalline solids, and Rydberg-dressed atoms, which in simulation form cluster (super)solids. We also vary the particle mass, i.e., the quantumness of the system, so as to modify the relative stability of ``solid'' and fluid states. We thus find a whole spectrum of (finite-size) phases with a curved structure, including multilayer and cluster phases, as well as superfluids and single layer supersolids. In particular, we confirm that supersolids only occur in the presence of clusters. By considering three system sizes (from 60 to 180 particles), but rescaling the trap radius so that the density stays fixed, we verify that supersolid states only exist in the same range of particle masses. Our model serves as a platform to test how emergent properties are modified, in spherical geometry, in the crossover from atoms to dressed atoms.
summary: This paper uses advanced simulations and theoretical analysis to map the quantum phase diagram of bosons in a spherical trap as the interparticle interaction softens. By analyzing superfluidity, clustering, and symmetry via the Spherical Structure Factor, the authors demonstrate a rich spectrum of phases, notably confirming that supersolid behavior requires the presence of underlying cluster structures.
main_problem: The study investigates how the equilibrium structure and superfluidity of spinless bosons trapped in a spherical shell change when the interparticle potential core is varied from hard-core to soft-core.
main_result: The research confirms that supersolid states only emerge when clusters are present, and these supersolid phases are restricted to a specific range of particle masses, regardless of the system size tested.
method: The study employs Path Integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations, supplemented by theoretical derivations relating correlation functions to the Spherical Structure Factor (SSF).
model_or_system: The system consists of spinless bosons confined in a broad spherical shell, governed by a Hamiltonian incorporating an external trapping potential and a tunable interparticle potential. The model bridges the physics of Helium-like atoms (hard-core) and Rydberg-dressed atoms (soft-core).
key_observables: Superfluid fraction ($f_s$), radial distribution function ($g(r)$), Cycle Length Distribution ($P(L)$), and the Spherical Structure Factor ($S_l$).
important_parameters: Core stiffness (tuned by $r_0$), particle mass ($\lambda$), and system size ($N=60, 120, 180$).
main_assumptions: The SSF derivation for clusters assumes Gaussian cluster centers at vertices of highly symmetric polyhedra (octahedron or icosahedron).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the radial density profile changing with interaction softness, and the SSF is shown to match theoretical predictions for icosahedral and octahedral cluster arrangements.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and simulation methods (PIMC) to map out the phase diagram based on interaction softness. It then develops the theoretical framework using spherical harmonics to calculate the SSF, confirming structural symmetries in the resulting phases.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, tunable platform to study the crossover between different quantum regimes (e.g., crystalline solids to superfluid/supersolids) in a geometrically constrained environment, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum matter in optical lattices or traps.
